messages:
maria: quick sync — findings from the multi-region failover load test this morning. found a kernel selection regression when we hit region B fallback traffic; need eyes on batching heuristics and KV cache behavior.

aj: saw p95 jump from 120ms -> 340ms after failover to region-b fallback model. GPU util stayed ~60% but token/sec dropped. suspect kernel fallback chaining + small-batch inefficiency.

kai: can you paste the exact harness config? was this a replay or synthetic?

maria: replay harness from prod traces (sanitized). we retargeted 10% of traffic to region-b to simulate outage in region-a. harness used `--keep-prefix-cache` for session affinity. synthetic runs didn't reproduce the full spike.

sophia: interesting that synthetic didn't reproduce. replay includes many short-turn convs with repeated prefixes — probably KV cache hit/miss pattern differs.

aj: profiling snippets: p95 120ms baseline (region-a). on region-b failover p95 340ms and median expanded slightly. GPU kernels switched from fast-fused-attn to fallback-mha at ~384 token lengths due to kernel selection heuristic hitting a branch.

maria: here's an excerpt from the perf trace (condensed):

```
[run 2026-03-16T09:11]
model: redwood-v2-16k-q4
region: region-b
kernel: fallback-mha
batch_size_effective: 3 (target 8)
kv_cache_misses: 42% of requests
latencies_ms: p50=95 p95=340 p99=520
gpu_util: 62% core_mem=78%
```

sophia: KV misses at 42% is big — replayed sessions losing KVs during routing transitions? that would force extra compute and change kernel paths (longer sequence lengths when prefix re-sent).

kai: on the routing side we drain region-a and route to region-b using consistent-hash fallback. we didn't preserve session KV pins in the failover rule — maybe that's the culprit.

aj: also noticed batching heuristics reduce effective batch size because requests arrive from multiple regions with different model variants; continuous-batching's packer rejects merging when kernel metadata differs. result: many small partial batches hitting fallback kernels.

maria: tl;dr: three interacting issues — routing-induced KV cold starts, kernel selection switching to slower kernels, and small-batch penalties.

perf-bot: benchmark job 1773002468-1 completed: replay 10k reqs, avg tokens/sec 850 -> 540 on failover.

aj: propose two-pronged test to confirm causality: (1) replay with session-pin preserved across region switch (force KV reuse), (2) synthetic that forces kernel path parity but keeps KV cold to isolate kernel selection impact.

sophia: agree. also add a run where we fake binary-compatible kernel metadata so the packer will batch across variants to measure batching loss.

kai: I can modify routing rules in the staging harness to include session pin header X-Session-Pin and a route rule that preserves that header during region failover.

maria: good. let's also capture continuous-batcher metrics: batch sizes histogram, batch-wait-time, packer mismatch count, and kernel-switch count per call.

aj: here's a quick packer config tweak to try in the harness to allow cross-variant batching (for testing only):

```
packer.allow_cross_variant = true
packer.variant_tolerance = 0.01
```

maria: run plan:
- run A (baseline replay, current harness) — already done
- run B (preserve session pin) — kai to run
- run C (synthetic kernel parity, KV cold) — aj/sophia
- run D (allow cross-variant batching) — aj

sophia: metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, avg batch size, kv_hit_rate, kernel_switches, gpu_util, rt_tail_percentile trends. also trace a couple of sample requests top-to-bottom.

kai: started run B on staging cluster now. will post results in ~12m. deploy-bot: starting canary to region-b for test run B.

deploy-bot: canary started — id: cb-1773002468-b. logs streaming.

aj: FYI we should keep model versions identical across regions (same compiled kernels). if there are differences in kernel compilation flags we get non-deterministic packer behavior. confirm build hashes.

maria: build hashes: region-a: 0f3a9c, region-b: 0f3a9c (matched). so not a compile mismatch.

sophia: OK, then routing header / KV loss and packer variant metadata look like primary suspects.

kai (12m later): run B results: p95 dropped to 140ms (from 340) when session pin preserved. kv_hit_rate increased to 88%. tokens/sec climbed back to ~800. batch size avg from 3 -> 7.

aj: confirms KV cold starts are driving most of the regression. kernel fallback still happens in ~3% of calls when sequence lengths grow beyond compiled thresholds, but impact small compared to KV effect.

maria: action items:
- kai: update failover routing to preserve session-pin header in staging + file a change for prod routing rules (JIRA: RT-1248).
- aj: add a lighter-touch packer heuristic to opportunistically batch across compatible variants (feature flag behind `packer.allow_cross_variant`). test impact and risks (JIRA: PERF-2310).
- sophia: add a KV-preservation test in the replay harness and include sample-request traces to validate end-to-end correctness.
- perf-bot: schedule full 100k replay overnight with session preservation on/off and store traces.

maria: also, let's not roll kernel fallback changes to production until we understand the 3% edge cases. small kernel changes can ripple into batchability.

aj: ack. I'll prepare a short doc with graphs comparing runs A/B/C/D and upload to the shared perf folder.

kai: will open the prod-routing PR and add a canary window.

maria: thanks all. if anyone sees a different hypothesis ping me. I'll ping infra to hold any kernel regression rollouts until we complete the tests. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: scheduled job 1773002468-2 (100k replay) for 2026-03-17T00:30 UTC.

maria: closing thread; please post results in this thread when jobs complete.
